videos.caption: While children around the world return to school, Gaza’s children are entering their third consecutive year without an education. More than 90% of schools in Gaza have been damaged or reduced to ruins amid Israel’s unrelenting genocide. 22,000+ Palestinian children slaughtered. 44,000+ injured. Thousands remain missing. Likely martyred and still beneath the rubble. While children elsewhere put on new uniforms, carry new school bags and look forward to seeing their friends, children in Gaza are fighting simply to survive. Children are deliberately sniped as target practice and killed including for flying kites. Childhood stolen. Thousands orphaned. Children have been forced into the role of parents, caring for younger siblings after their parents martyred. The suffering doesn't stop at Gaza. In the West Bank, 84 Palestinian schools currently face demolition or orders to stop educating, leaving almost 13,000 students uncertain whether their schools will exist tomorrow. All of this unfolding against the backdrop of Israel’s continuing occupation and expansion of illegal settlements. For Palestinian children, school should mean learning, not survival. Childhood should mean safety, not fear. The children of Palestine have been deprived of their right to an education and the world has sadly failed to protect it. #freepalestine #stopthegenocide #palestine #gaza #westbank

Is Palestine a country, or !sr@el ? To understand the answer, you have to understand the history. This five-part series traces the history of Palestine from the Ottoman era through the British Mandate, the Balfour Declaration, the 1947 UN Partition Plan, the Nakba of 1948, the 1967 Six-Day War, the occupation, the First and Second Intifadas, the Oslo Accords, the blockade of Gaza, and the events following October 7, 2023. We explore how Palestine changed politically and geographically, how hundreds of thousands of Palestinians became refugees, how !sr@el was established, how the occupation began, and why Palestinian statehood remains unresolved today. The final part answers the central question: Is Palestine a country? This is the history of Palestine, !sr@el, the Palestinian people, and one of the world's longest-running conflicts, explained from beginning to present day.
